source_trace.observation: ParticleIndex assigns a role without proving membership. Arity is nonzero, flat records must be complete, ordered upload emits one u32 word per particle address and substitutes an empty word only for an empty upload. ConstraintEdges supplies pairs.

The generic constructor receives an Arc<Kernel> and incidence separately, derives coloring and uploads that incidence, and stores kernel and arity without a shown check that the selected kernel consumes that record width. The selected distance constructor obtains pair incidence and checks rest-length count. Solve returns early for disabled or empty sets, binds buffers and dispatches nonempty color ranges.
DISTANCE is shader source text declaring two particle indices per constraint and referring to 2*constraint and 2*constraint+1. It was not compiled or executed.
Element upload is a byte slice; the minimum word is substituted only when empty.
The displayed generic upload allocates from upload length; native allocation, binding validation and read outcome are not demonstrated.
Coloring is built from incidence records, assigns conflicts by particle address and accumulates/prefixes u32 ConstraintSlot counters.
ConstraintCount retains usize but displayed native uniform and dispatch conversions narrow to u32; lambda byte allocation has a separate conversion.

The selected Shell path validates mesh and material, constructs stretch/seams via distance pair records and builds explicit four-particle bending incidence; it is not a witness of the hypothetical distance/arity-one pairing.

conditional_candidate.classification: If an otherwise admissible custom caller can pair the distance kernel with a complete one-record arity-one incidence and its other required bindings, and a nonempty solve reaches the shader, the shown populated upload contains one particle word while DISTANCE source refers to logical words 0 and 1 for constraint zero. This is a source-level mismatch of the selected layouts, not proof of a dispatched call, successful native binding or a particular GPU result.
